questions.q: From Setup, which Quick Find item opens the table of recent configuration changes, including sharing-model changes like OWD edits and sharing rule creation?
options: Login History
View Setup Audit Trail
Health Check
Field History Tracking
questions.explain: View Setup Audit Trail logs configuration changes made in Setup — permission edits, security setting changes, and sharing-model changes among them — automatically, with no setup required.

questions.q: How much setup-change history can an admin download as a CSV from Setup Audit Trail, beyond the 20 entries shown on screen?
options: 30 days
90 days
Six months
Indefinitely, with no limit
questions.explain: The on-screen view holds only the most recent 20 entries; the download link provides the full six months of history as a CSV for anything older.

questions.q: A sharing recalculation job triggered by an OWD change writes what into Setup Audit Trail?
options: Nothing — recalculation jobs run silently and leave no record
Only a single entry once the job finishes, with no start time
An email to the admin, not an audit trail entry
A pair of Initiated and Completed entries with timestamps, usable to confirm the job ran and how long it took
questions.explain: Recalculation jobs write their own Initiated and Completed rows into the audit trail, which is what makes the trail useful for confirming a recalculation actually completed rather than just assuming it did.

questions.q: A manager asks why a specific user can see one specific Opportunity record right now. What's the fastest way to get a definitive answer?
options: Open that record's sharing detail page and read the listed access level and reason
Re-derive the answer by re-reading the OWD grid from scratch
Wait for the next scheduled sharing recalculation job to run
Check Login History for that user's most recent login
questions.explain: A record's own sharing detail page lists every user/group with access, their access level, and the specific reason (owner, role, rule, team, manual share, Apex), skipping the need to re-derive the computed result from scratch.

questions.q: What does Setup's Health Check tool actually evaluate, and how does it relate to a sharing-model audit?
options: It scores the sharing model directly and replaces the need to check OWD or sharing rules
It scores org-wide security settings like password and session policies against a baseline, and is a useful adjacent habit but not a sharing-model review itself
It is identical to Setup Audit Trail, just under a different name
It only applies to Experience Cloud sites, not internal users
questions.explain: Health Check scores security settings such as password policies and session settings against Salesforce's baseline. It doesn't evaluate the sharing model itself, but running it on the same cadence as sharing audits keeps access review from being the only security check happening.
